title: Unconstrained orthogonal Kabsch alignment returns improper inversion rotations unless determinant sign is enforced
paper_label: Kabsch (1978) Acta Crystallogr. Sect. A 34, 827
claimed: Minimizing weighted squared coordinate deviations over all orthogonal matrices via Kabsch (1976) is sometimes implemented without checking covariance determinant sign when computing macromolecular RMSD collective variables.
corrected: Stationary orthogonal solutions of U(S + L) = R in Kabsch (1976) produce improper orthogonal transformations with determinant minus one whenever the cross covariance matrix R has negative determinant, inverting chiral biomolecular structures. Kabsch (1978) negates the singular vector contribution paired with the smallest eigenvalue of R transpose R whenever det(R) < 0, guaranteeing a proper unit determinant 3D rotation.

events.author: Evangelos A. Coutsias
events.text: Coutsias, Seok and Dill (2004) reformulate proper weighted macromolecular RMSD minimization via quaternions and compare singular value sign conventions against Kabsch (1976) and Kabsch (1978).

events.author: Jim Lawrence
events.text: Lawrence, Bernal and Witzgall (2019) establish an algebraic justification of the Kabsch Umeyama proper rotation singular value decomposition correcting improper reflections across arbitrary dimensions.

title: Finite q-sphere trajectory truncation biases bimolecular k_on without the Northrup-Allison-McCammon re-entry correction
paper_label: Northrup, Allison & McCammon (1984) J. Chem. Phys. 80, 1517
claimed: Terminating Brownian association trajectories at a finite outer radius q > b and equating simulated capture fraction beta_1 with infinite-volume reaction probability beta_infinity omits diffusive walkers reaching radius q that re-cross the inner b-sphere prior to escaping to infinity.
corrected: Exact Smoluchowski flux matching beyond the centrosymmetric b-sphere corrects finite-q truncation through beta_infinity = beta_1 / [1-(1-beta_1)Omega] with re-entry probability Omega = k(b)/k(q) = b/q for isotropic outer diffusion, recovering k_on = k(b) beta_infinity.

events.author: Gary Huber
events.text: Embeds unbiased Weighted Ensemble walker splitting and merging between the Northrup-Allison-McCammon b and q spheres to resolve rare electrostatically steered protein encounters.

events.author: Atipat Rojnuckarin
events.text: Implements Weighted Ensemble Brownian dynamics within University of Houston Brownian Dynamics across Northrup-Allison-McCammon reaction surfaces.

events.author: Ali Sinan Saglam
events.text: Couples steady-state Northrup-Allison-McCammon Weighted Ensemble with flexible coarse-grained barnase-barstar Brownian dynamics and hydrodynamic interactions to compute basal k_on = (2.85 +- 1.30) x 10^6 M^-1 s^-1.

events.author: Robert Hall
events.text: Contrasts Northrup-Allison-McCammon outer-sphere unbound sampling against finite periodic-box rebinding corrections in explicit-solvent host-guest simulations.

title: Finite-box periodic Oseen drag and low TIP3P viscosity introduce opposing biases in explicit-solvent bimolecular k_on
paper_label: Yeh & Hummer (2004) J. Phys. Chem. B 108, 15873
claimed: Explicit-solvent bimolecular k_on Weighted Ensemble simulations report raw periodic-box association rates without adding the Yeh-Hummer Ewald hydrodynamic self-diffusion term, while Saglam & Chong (2019) misprinted the 1.7 mM barnase-barstar box volume in units of 956 A^3 rather than 956 nm^3.
corrected: Periodic lattice hydrodynamic interactions retard each diffusing partner by k_B T xi / (6 pi eta L) with cubic Ewald constant xi = 2.837297, partially masking the 2.5-fold excess diffusivity of TIP3P water, while 1.7 mM single-pair concentration corresponds to V_box = 956 nm^3 (L = 9.85 nm).

events.author: Efrem Braun
events.text: Codifies analytical Yeh-Hummer periodic box diffusivity corrections and Green-Kubo viscosity checks for molecular transport simulations.

events.author: Tadashi Ando
events.text: Applies Yeh-Hummer system-size scaling alongside Green-Kubo shear viscosity calculations across OPC and OPC3 water models from 273 K to 373 K.

events.author: Ashlin James Poruthoor
events.text: Evaluates periodic box-dimension artifacts on free-energy barriers and lateral dynamics in phase-separating lipid bilayers.

title: Unordered systematic resampling fails unconditional variance dominance and large sample error decay
paper_label: Douc, Cappe & Moulines (2005) Proc. ISPA, 64
claimed: Sequential Monte Carlo and trajectory stratification workflows frequently treat systematic single uniform resampling like a universally lower variance replacement for multinomial and stratified resampling regardless of walker ordering.
corrected: Douc, Cappe and Moulines (2005) prove that residual and Kitagawa (1996) stratified resampling strictly dominate multinomial resampling in conditional variance for every measurable observable, whereas systematic resampling admits explicit particle ordering counterexamples exceeding multinomial variance and failing to vanish in the large particle limit unless walkers are pre ordered along state coordinates or a Hilbert curve.

events.author: Mathieu Gerber
events.text: Gerber, Chopin and Whiteley (2019) note that unordered systematic resampling variance can fail to converge to zero per Douc et al. (2005), while proving almost sure weak convergence for Kitagawa (1996) stratified resampling and o(N^{-(1+1/d)}) variance under d dimensional Hilbert curve ordering.

events.author: John Strahan
events.text: Strahan, Lorpaiboon, Weare and Dinner (2024) incorporate variance reduced resampling protocols analyzed by Douc, Cappe and Moulines (2005) within BAD NEUS trajectory stratification.

title: Transition event duration density requires splitting probability normalization and global barrier shape
paper_label: Zhang, Jasnow & Zuckerman (2007) J. Chem. Phys. 126, 074504
claimed: Barrier crossing event durations are frequently approximated from harmonic barrier top curvature alone or confounded with unconditioned absorbing boundary exit currents.
corrected: Under two sided absorbing boundaries on [a, b], nearly all trajectories released at a + epsilon absorb back at a, requiring conditional normalization of exit current J(b, t) by the vanishing splitting probability Pi_b(a + epsilon). Mean event duration depends on global anharmonic potential shape through the path integral effective potential V(x) rather than barrier top curvature alone.

events.author: Zhang, Jasnow & Zuckerman
events.text: Connects finite transition event durations to Weighted Ensemble path sampling of united residue calmodulin conformational switching.

events.author: Donovan Maiye et al.
events.text: Designates the intrinsic transition event duration t_b of Zhang, Jasnow and Zuckerman 2007 a hard lower timescale bound on accelerated nonequilibrium sampling.

events.author: DeGrave, Bogetti & Chong
events.text: Incorporates the empirical event duration distribution into pre steady state Weighted Ensemble rate estimation via the RED scheme.

title: Duplicate citation and author order reversal between arXiv 0810.1963 and 2010 JCP exactness theorem
paper_label: Zhang, Jasnow & Zuckerman (2010) J. Chem. Phys. 132, 054107
claimed: Downstream documentation and bibliographies cite arXiv 0810.1963 Section II.F alongside Zhang, Jasnow and Zuckerman (2010) under two separate entries, and invoke path space resampling exactness under adaptive bins without stating the stochastic trajectory divergence requirement.
corrected: Preprint arXiv 0810.1963 and J. Chem. Phys. 132, 054107 (2010) represent one work whose author sequence changed from Zhang, Zuckerman, Jasnow on arXiv to Zhang, Jasnow, Zuckerman in print, proving exact path ensemble preservation across Markovian, non Markovian, and adaptive bin protocols whenever daughter walkers evolve under independent stochastic increments and resampling conserves conditional weight expectation.

events.author: Rory Donovan Maiye
events.text: Donovan Maiye et al. (2013) apply exact path space resampling with non overlapping static and dynamic tessellations to Gillespie chemical reaction networks without altering underlying stochastic path probabilities.

events.author: David Aristoff
events.text: Aristoff, Bello Rivas and Elber (2016) group Weighted Ensemble path resampling alongside Exact Milestoning, Transition Interface Sampling, Forward Flux Sampling, and Non Equilibrium Umbrella Sampling among unbiased rare event stratification frameworks.

title: Steady state bin reweighting requires fast orthogonal intra bin relaxation
paper_label: Bhatt, Zhang & Zuckerman (2010) J. Chem. Phys. 133, 014110
claimed: Enhanced steady state Weighted Ensemble reweighting (WESS) replaces exact regional flux conservation sum_j f_ji = sum_j f_ij with a first order Markov bin rate balance sum_j k_ji P_j = sum_j k_ij P_i to rescale walker weights.
corrected: Markovian bin rescaling accelerates convergence strictly when simulation bins capture all slow reaction coordinates. Unresolved orthogonal barriers or hidden metastable intermediates inside coarse bins corrupt inter bin rate estimates k_ij, contributing to multi decade rate discrepancies in internal cavity unbinding.
math_tex: \sum_j \bigl(f_{ji}^{\mathrm{SS}} - f_{ij}^{\mathrm{SS}}\bigr) = 0 \;\xRightarrow{\text{Markov bin closure}}\; \sum_j \bigl(k_{ji} P_j^{\mathrm{SS}} - k_{ij} P_i^{\mathrm{SS}}\bigr) = 0

events.author: Donovan Maiye et al.
events.text: Adopts Bhatt et al. 2010 inter bin rate matrix reweighting under the assumption that f_ij = k_ij w_j holds both in and out of steady state.

events.author: Aristoff & Zuckerman
events.text: Derives first principles variance minimizing bin partitions and walker allocations for steady state Weighted Ensemble sampling.

events.author: Copperman & Zuckerman
events.text: Points out that practical Weighted Ensemble runs sustain tens to hundreds of bins, remaining too coarse for unbiased Markov rate closure prior to relaxation.

events.author: Kania et al.
events.text: Eliminates the fixed bin Markovian closure of WESS by rotating random hyperplane tessellations across RiteWeight iterations.

title: Standard nonparametric bootstrap downward biases lower confidence bounds on heavy tailed replicate rates
paper_label: Mostofian & Zuckerman (2019) J. Chem. Theory Comput. 15, 3499
claimed: Rate uncertainties across Weighted Ensemble runs are often reported via sample mean plus or minus standard error or standard Efron nonparametric bootstrap intervals on 5 to 15 replicates.
corrected: Genealogical walker correlations necessitate independent Weighted Ensemble runs, and atomistic folding rates across 13 Protein G or 15 NTL9 runs span 20 to 70 orders of magnitude. Whenever base 10 log standard deviation exceeds unity, symmetric standard error intervals cross below zero, standard nonparametric bootstrap over weights resamples omitting rare high flux runs to produce an artificial downward log space lower bound cliff, and nominal 95 percent intervals of both standard and Dirichlet Bayesian bootstraps miss the true mean in roughly 30 percent of synthetic benchmarks.

events.author: Daniel M. Zuckerman
events.text: Zuckerman and Russo (2021) incorporate the small sample high log variance uncertainty cautions of Mostofian and Zuckerman (2019) into pedagogical guidance on non equilibrium trajectory ensemble rate estimation.

title: Monotonic Smoluchowski current bounds break in multidimensional or inertial Langevin dynamics
paper_label: Copperman, Aristoff, Makarov, Simpson & Zuckerman (2019) J. Chem. Phys. 151, 214108
claimed: Spatial extrema of transient probability currents are invoked to bracket steady state flux monotonically from above and below and to diagnose convergence from a flat reaction coordinate flux profile.
corrected: The parabolic maximum principle guaranteeing monotonic contraction of min_x J(x,t) and max_x J(x,t) holds for one dimensional overdamped Smoluchowski diffusion. Explicit two dimensional potentials violate monotonic decay of maximum current magnitude, and inertial Langevin dynamics require momentum relaxation before overdamped Smoluchowski recycling bounds apply.
math_tex: \min_{0 \le x \le x_{\mathrm{src}}} J(x, t_1) \le \min_{0 \le x \le x_{\mathrm{src}}} J(x, t_2) \le J_{\mathrm{SS}} \le \max_{0 \le x \le x_{\mathrm{src}}} J(x, t_2) \le \max_{0 \le x \le x_{\mathrm{src}}} J(x, t_1)

events.author: Aristoff & Zuckerman
events.text: Replaces continuum 1D Smoluchowski heuristics with discrete time Doob martingale variance minimization on general Borel Markov kernels.

events.author: Copperman & Zuckerman
events.text: Propagates inertial second order 2D Langevin trajectories while approximating continuum recycling via the overdamped Smoluchowski PDE.

events.author: Copperman & Zuckerman
events.text: Motivates microbin haMSM steady state extraction from slow pre steady state current relaxation across multidimensional biomolecular coordinates.

title: Barnase barstar box volume printed in cubic Angstroms rather than cubic nanometers at 1.7 mM
paper_label: Saglam & Chong (2019) Chem. Sci. 10, 2360
claimed: The published article prints the explicit solvent simulation box volume at 956 A^3 next to a reactant concentration of 1.7 mM, and downstream citations classify the calculation under steady state Weighted Ensemble sampling.
corrected: One protein pair at 1.7 mM requires roughly 977 nm^3, confirming that 956 A^3 (0.956 nm^3, corresponding to 1.74 M) is a thousandfold unit typo for 956 nm^3. Subsequent Chong lab reanalysis in DeGrave, Bogetti and Chong 2021 documents a single 650 iteration (18 us) unrecycled equilibrium Weighted Ensemble run.

events.author: Ray & Andricioaei
events.text: Benchmarks Weighted Ensemble Milestoning against the explicit solvent barnase barstar association rate constant of Saglam and Chong 2019.

events.author: Ray et al.
events.text: Classifies Saglam and Chong 2019 under steady state Weighted Ensemble rate calculations, whereas DeGrave et al. 2021 documents a single equilibrium run.

events.author: DeGrave, Bogetti & Chong
events.text: Reanalyzes the single 650 iteration (tau = 20 ps, 18 us) equilibrium Weighted Ensemble dataset of Saglam and Chong 2019 via RED across a 6 ns event duration.

events.author: Dommer et al.
events.text: Cites Saglam and Chong 2019 atomistic protein protein association pathways when scaling Weighted Ensemble workflows to viral spike assemblies.

title: REVO pairwise variation optimization removes Voronoi region walls while requiring quasi unbound cloning cutoffs and merging bias corrections
paper_label: Donyapour, Roussey & Dickson (2019) J. Chem. Phys. 150, 244112
claimed: Hierarchical Voronoi tessellations in WExplore enforce hard multi level distance thresholds that trigger discontinuous walker cloning across region walls, whereas unconstrained pairwise distance variation maximization continues splitting quasi unbound ligand trajectories into tiny weight exits.
corrected: Resampling of Ensembles by Variation Optimization (REVO) optimizes global pairwise trajectory distance variation weighted by logarithmic walker novelty phi_i(w_i), recovering a 3.76 ms trypsin benzamidine residence time (experiment 1.6 ms) and a fourth exit pathway, while subsequent audits add finite volume rate ratio corrections, quasi unbound cloning cutoffs, and merging bias corrected Markov models.

events.author: Andrea Rizzi
events.text: SAMPL6 blind challenge comparisons report standard REVO rate ratio binding free energies 5 to 6 kcal/mol more negative than alchemical benchmarks with elevated replicate spread on OA G3.

events.author: Robert Hall
events.text: Derives finite simulation box volume and state boundary free energy correction terms for REVO transition path rate ratios, cutting SAMPL6 OA G6 discrepancy relative to alchemical benchmarks from 3.4 to 0.76 kcal/mol.

events.author: Nicole M. Roussey
events.text: Identifies variation inflation from large pairwise distances in quasi unbound states and blocks quasi unbound cloning in Cutoff REVO, lowering SAMPL6 CB8 G3 free energy uncertainty from 1.01 to 0.13 kcal/mol.

events.author: Samik Bose
events.text: Identifies trajectory merging bias in Markov state models constructed from REVO ensembles at lag intervals exceeding the Weighted Ensemble resampling step and introduces MBC MSMs.

title: Misreported Protein G experimental folding time and unrelaxed flux corrected in 2021 JACS erratum
paper_label: Adhikari et al. (2019) J. Am. Chem. Soc. 141, 6519
claimed: Table 1 and Figure 4 reported an experimental Protein G B1 domain folding time near 1 s after misinterpreting denaturant and pH conditions, alongside unrelaxed raw Weighted Ensemble flux estimates of 4 to 210 s across 15 implicit-solvent runs.
corrected: Adhikari et al. (2021) J. Am. Chem. Soc. 143, 7588 corrected the zero-denaturant experimental Protein G folding time to 2 to 40 ms (3.1 ms at pH 4.0 to 39 ms at pH 11.2), matching the history-augmented Markov state model estimate of 3.3 to 200 ms and the restarted Weighted Ensemble interval of 0.3 to 4.3 ms.

events.author: Barmak Mostofian
events.text: Reanalysis of the 13 Protein G Weighted Ensemble runs documents flux estimates spanning 70 orders of magnitude where nominal 95 percent bootstrap intervals miss the true mean in roughly 30 percent of synthetic trials.

events.author: Dhiman Ray
events.text: Repeats the framing that microsecond Weighted Ensemble trajectories captured millisecond to second atomistic folding kinetics for NTL9 and Protein G prior to the 2021 experimental benchmark erratum.

events.author: Jeremy Copperman
events.text: Flags the experimental Protein G folding time printed in Adhikari et al. (2019) to be erroneous while diagnosing slow steady-state relaxation across long-lived folding intermediates.

events.author: Jeremy Copperman
events.text: Restarts Weighted Ensemble trajectories from microbin history-augmented Markov steady-state weights, raising Protein G folding flux three orders of magnitude to a 0.3 to 4.3 ms folding time consistent with pH 4.0 to 11.2 measurements.

events.author: Won Hee Ryu
events.text: Constructs discrepancy and local variance optimized bins from history-augmented Markov models on high-friction NTL9 folding, narrowing run-to-run flux spread from 35 orders of magnitude down to 12 orders.

title: Milestone transition kernel eigenvectors require lifetime weighting and equilibrated hypersurface ensembles
paper_label: Ray & Andricioaei (2020) J. Chem. Phys.
claimed: Naive milestoning implementations interpret the principal stationary eigenvector of the milestone to milestone transition kernel to be equilibrium milestone probability and launch Weighted Ensemble Milestoning runs from a single structure per milestone.
corrected: In Weighted Ensemble Milestoning building upon Faradjian and Elber (2004), the unit eigenvalue row eigenvector of the milestone transition kernel K represents stationary milestone hitting flux rather than equilibrium probability, requiring element wise multiplication by mean milestone lifetime T_i. Launching independent runs from a single configuration per milestone undersamples orthogonal degrees of freedom on multidimensional protein ligand milestones and inflates dissociation rate and free energy spread.

events.author: Dhiman Ray
events.text: Ray, Gokey, Mobley and Andricioaei (2020) report high variability in FKBP butyl ligand dissociation free energies and off rates under single structure milestone seeding in standard Weighted Ensemble Milestoning, introducing harmonic restraint release milestone ensembles.

title: Unmarked coarse Markov matrices mix directional ensembles resolved by history labeled microbins
paper_label: Copperman & Zuckerman (2020) J. Chem. Theory Comput. 16, 6763
claimed: Unmarked Markov transition matrices built on tens or hundreds of simulation bins pool trajectories last in reactant state A with trajectories last in product state B, biasing first passage rate estimates prior to full steady state relaxation.
corrected: Decomposing populations into two color history labeled alpha and beta ensembles and post clustering short pre steady state Weighted Ensemble segments into fine microbin haMSM operators T_ij^alpha with sink to source recycling T_ba = 1 recovers unbiased steady state k_AB before ensemble relaxation.
math_tex: p_i^{\mathrm{eq}} = p_i^{\alpha} + p_i^{\beta}, \qquad k_{AB} = \sum_{i \notin B,\, j \in B} p_i^{\alpha} T_{ij}^{\alpha}, \quad T_{ij}^{\alpha} = \mathbb{P}(X_{t+\tau}^{\alpha} = j \mid X_t^{\alpha} = i)

events.author: Pratt et al.
events.text: Demonstrates across methane, Na+/Cl-, and K+/18 crown 6 benchmarks that history tracking and post simulation haMSM analysis accelerate k_on, k_off, and K_D convergence.

events.author: Copperman & Zuckerman
events.text: Formulates the one way alpha ensemble transition submatrix with explicit sink to source boundary recycling T_ba = 1 on fine microstate partitions.

events.author: Dommer et al.
events.text: Implements parallelized streaming haMSM microbin rate estimation for terabyte scale glycosylated Delta spike opening trajectories.

events.author: Strahan et al.
events.text: Builds upon Copperman and Zuckerman 2020 unbiased splitting segment haMSM construction when formulating BAD NEUS stratification.

title: Variance optimal steady state allocation scales with bin weight times discrepancy standard deviation rather than uniform walkers per bin
paper_label: Aristoff & Zuckerman (2020) Multiscale Model. Simul. 18, 646
claimed: Classical Weighted Ensemble protocols allocate an identical walker count N_t(u) = M to every occupied bin, expending parallel trajectories in off pathway or flat committor basins where splitting fails to reduce target flux variance.
corrected: Martingale variance decomposition across selection and mutation steps proves via Lagrange multipliers that asymptotic steady state flux variance is minimized when bin allocation scales with bin weight omega_t(u) times intrabin one step flux discrepancy standard deviation sigma_t(u), corresponding to continuous steady state trajectory density proportional to pi(x) v(x).

events.author: Robert J. Webber
events.text: Transfers discrepancy based variance minimization from Weighted Ensemble bin allocation to splitting accelerated Markov chain Monte Carlo.

events.author: Paul A. Torrillo
events.text: Contrasts coarse model variance minimization binning against zero prior heuristic bottleneck isolation in Minimal Adaptive Binning.

events.author: David Aristoff
events.text: Expresses flux discrepancy via local mean first passage times and demonstrates on a two dimensional Smoluchowski surface that equal pi*v discrepancy bins cut normalized flux variance by 3 to 5 orders of magnitude over radial bins while radial bins underperform brute force.

events.author: Won Hee Ryu
events.text: Applies haMSM estimated equal pi*v discrepancy bins to atomistic NTL9 protein folding at water like friction, compressing replicate flux spread from 35 orders of magnitude to 12 orders of magnitude.

title: Unconstrained REVO cloning in quasi unbound states and walker merge pruning in wepy bias naive rate ratio affinities
paper_label: Lotz & Dickson (2020) ACS Omega 5, 31608
claimed: Regionless REVO and WExplore simulations in wepy generate thousands of ligand exit trajectories whose raw transition counts and steady state rate ratios k_off / k_on are sometimes plugged straight into Markov state models or free energy formulas.
corrected: WepyHDF5 records explicit cloning and merging lineage graphs where pruned walkers transfer weight w_i + w_j to surviving clones with probability w_i / (w_i + w_j), truncating losing branches in unweighted transition counts. In addition, unconstrained REVO cloning inside quasi unbound regions inflates SAMPL6 host guest binding free energy errors until boundary committor corrections and Cutoff REVO cloning thresholds are applied.
math_tex: \mathbb{P}(\text{retain } i \mid \text{merge } i,j) = \frac{w_i}{w_i + w_j}, \qquad w_{\mathrm{surv}} = w_i + w_j

events.author: Nicole M. Roussey
events.text: Reconstructs continuous reactive exit lineages from WepyHDF5 trees to demonstrate six order of magnitude higher SAMPL6 unbinding path probabilities under depleted pocket Na+ density.

events.author: Nicole M. Roussey
events.text: Identifies excess cloning in quasi unbound states of standard REVO inside wepy and introduces Cutoff REVO to improve SAMPL6 and SAMPL9 binding free energies.

events.author: John D. Russo
events.text: Incorporates a generalized binless resampler interface in WESTPA 2.0 modeled on modular resampler abstractions in wepy.

title: Uncorrected rate-ratio binding free energies omit finite-box volume, state-boundary, and residual electrostatic terms
paper_label: Hall, Dixon & Dickson (2020) Front. Mol. Biosci. 7, 106
claimed: SAMPL6 host-guest REVO submissions computed standard binding free energies from raw k_off over k_on ratios without accounting for finite periodic box volume, unbound state definition volume, or residual host-guest electrostatic coupling at the 1 nm cutoff, overbinding OA-G6 at -12.1 kcal/mol against the -7.0 kcal/mol alchemical reference.
corrected: Deriving analytical volume, state-boundary, and screened electrostatic corrections for reactive trajectory ensembles cuts the OA-G6 binding free energy error relative to computational benchmarks from 3.4 kcal/mol down to 0.76 kcal/mol.

events.author: Dhiman Ray
events.text: Computes trypsin-benzamidine association rate, dissociation rate, and standard binding free energy simultaneously through continuous Voronoi-cell Markovian Weighted Ensemble Milestoning.

events.author: Nicole M. Roussey
events.text: Reanalyzes OA-G3 and OA-G6 REVO transition paths from Dixon et al. (2018) and Hall et al. (2020), finding up to 10^6-fold higher unbinding path weights when sodium ion density drops above the host pocket.

events.author: Nicole M. Roussey
events.text: Introduces Cutoff-REVO to halt walker cloning in quasi-unbound regions, bringing OA-G6 to -5.21 kcal/mol and prospective SAMPL9 beta-cyclodextrin promazine affinity to -5.00 +- 0.66 kcal/mol against -4.97 kcal/mol experiment.

events.author: Samik Bose
events.text: Eliminates asymmetric walker merging bias when building Markov state models from REVO ligand unbinding ensembles.

title: Extraneous molar factor in k_on and inverted thermodynamic signs in printed standard binding free energy equations
paper_label: Ray et al. (2020) J. Chem. Phys. 153, 065101
claimed: Equation 10 multiplies inverse binding mean first-passage time by dimensionless v c^0 N_av rather than molar box volume v N_av, while Equations 12 and 15 print Delta G^0 = -k_B T ln K_D for dissociation constant K_D and Delta G^0 = +k_B T ln(K_bind C^0) for association constant K_bind, inverting both standard-state signs.
corrected: Under the 1 M standard state (C^0 = 1 M, V^0 = 1 / (C^0 N_A) = 1661 A^3) established by Gilson et al. (1997) and Boresch et al. (2003), bimolecular k_on is V_box N_A / <tau>_on in M^-1 s^-1 and favorable complexation satisfies Delta G^0 = +k_B T ln(K_D / C^0) = -k_B T ln(K_bind C^0).
math_tex: k_{\mathrm{on}} = \frac{V_{\mathrm{box}} N_A}{\langle \tau \rangle_{\mathrm{on}}}, \qquad \Delta G^\circ = k_B T \ln\!\left(\frac{k_{\mathrm{off}}\,C^\circ}{k_{\mathrm{on}}}\right) = -k_B T \ln\!\left(\frac{K_{\mathrm{bind}}}{V^\circ}\right)

events.author: Dhiman Ray
events.text: Replaces milestone-reset Weighted Ensemble Milestoning with Markovian Weighted Ensemble Milestoning (M-WEM) to recover consistent negative binding free energies and millisecond residence times on trypsin-benzamidine.

events.author: Anthony T. Bogetti
events.text: Packages Markovian Weighted Ensemble Milestoning into WESTPA 2.0 Tutorial 7.9 alongside Colvars collective-variable restraints.

events.author: Marion Silvestrini
events.text: Compares milestoning dissociation strategies against three-stage Minimal Adaptive Binning steady-state Weighted Ensemble for THS-017 escape from the interior HIF-2alpha PAS-B cavity.

category: Pre steady state flux & event durations
title: RED event duration conditioning corrects twofold pre steady state flux underestimation
paper_label: DeGrave, Bogetti & Chong (2021) J. Chem. Phys. 154, 114111
claimed: Conventional pre steady state Weighted Ensemble flux estimators divide cumulative target arrival weight by total elapsed wall time t_max, implicitly assuming unit cumulative barrier crossing probability from t = 0 and overrepresenting anomalously fast crossings.
corrected: Replacing raw observation time with the time integrated cumulative event duration distribution H_AB(t) in the Rate from Event Durations (RED) estimator eliminates twofold transient underestimation in calbindin switching from the initial 25 percent of simulation data and improves barnase barstar k_on efficiency by at least 25 percent.

events.author: Zhang, Jasnow & Zuckerman
events.text: Derives the absorbing boundary Fokker Planck distribution rho_b(t) of finite barrier crossing event durations much shorter than first passage times.

events.author: Copperman et al.
events.text: Proves via a parabolic maximum principle on Smoluchowski currents that source initiated transient flux bounds true steady state flux from below during ramp up.

events.author: Saglam & Chong
events.text: Estimates explicit solvent barnase barstar association rates from cumulative Weighted Ensemble flux prior to RED event duration correction across a 6 ns crossing timescale.

events.author: Strahan et al.
events.text: Cites DeGrave, Bogetti and Chong 2021 when comparing pre steady state rate extraction against nonequilibrium trajectory stratification.

title: Minimal Adaptive Binning isolates uphill bottlenecks and avoids unoccupied manual rectilinear grid bins
paper_label: Torrillo, Bogetti & Chong (2021) J. Phys. Chem. A 125, 1642
claimed: Manual rectilinear grids partition d progress coordinates into M_1 x ... x M_d static hyperrectangles. On the two dimensional p53 peptide benchmark, manual grids populated 50 of 294 bins (17 percent occupancy) with 244 unoccupied cells, starving uphill barrier slopes and missing rare alpha_L helix and polyproline II conformations.
corrected: Minimal Adaptive Binning (MAB) brackets active outer progress extrema each iteration, subdivides the occupied interior into N_lin linear intervals, and assigns dedicated single walker bins to lagging, leading, and uphill bottleneck trajectories maximizing the log weight forward sum gap, raising p53 bin occupancy to 66 percent (29 of 44 bins) and Na+/Cl- association rate efficiency S_k from 3.1 to 5.1.
math_tex: i_{\mathrm{bottleneck}} = \arg\max_{i} \left( \log w_i - \log \sum_{j \succ i} w_j \right), \qquad N_{\mathrm{grid}}(d) = \prod_{k=1}^{d} M_k

events.author: John D. Russo
events.text: Integrates MAB into WESTPA 2.0 and achieves tacrine POPC membrane permeation flux two orders of magnitude higher than fixed rectilinear bins.

events.author: Abigail C. Dommer
events.text: Applies automated MAB uphill bottleneck isolation to accelerate Delta coronaviral spike opening across multimillion atom GPU ensembles.

events.author: Anthony T. Bogetti
events.text: Documents exponential coordinate product scaling and rule breaking trajectory merges in multidimensional rectilinear MAB during kinesin Eg5 ADP dissociation, motivating binless MABL scoring.

events.author: Jacky Chen
events.text: Formalizes MAB uphill bottleneck selection alongside semigroup consistent neural committor learning inside Weighted Ensemble loops.

title: Reversible Markov state models bias folding MFPTs below 100 ns lag whereas haMSMs hold at frame interval
paper_label: Suarez, Wiewiora, Wehmeyer, Noe, Chodera & Zuckerman (2021) J. Chem. Theory Comput. 17, 3119
claimed: Standard Markov state model workflows validate state partitions through implied relaxation timescales and enforce reversible detailed balance across pooled forward and backward transitions, assuming nanosecond lag matrices reproduce path observables.
corrected: Across Chignolin, Trp cage, Villin, and NTL9 folding trajectories, variationally validated PyEMMA models require lag times near 100 ns before mean first passage times converge, whereas history augmented Markov state models separate alpha and beta last macrostate ensembles without detailed balance symmetrization and recover reference mean first passage times at the molecular dynamics frame interval.
math_tex: \frac{1}{\mathrm{MFPT}_{A \to B}} = \frac{1}{p(\alpha)\,\Delta t}\sum_{i \notin B}\sum_{j \in B} \pi_i^{\alpha} T_{ij}^{\alpha}, \qquad \pi_i^{\alpha} T_{ij}^{\alpha} \neq \pi_j^{\alpha} T_{ji}^{\alpha}

events.author: John D. Russo
events.text: Proves analytically that coarse transition matrices recover exact microscopic mean first passage times when source sink recycling boundary conditions precede transition counting.

events.author: Darian T. Yang

title: Russo et al. 2021 remains an unpublished arXiv preprint establishing source sink coarse MSM and committor conditions
paper_label: Russo, Copperman, Aristoff, Simpson & Zuckerman (2021) arXiv 2105.13402
claimed: Downstream documentation and rate chapters cite Russo et al. 2021 like a peer reviewed journal article and invoke coarse first step committor equations Q_m = sum_n T_mn Q_n or equilibrium transition matrices for mean first passage times.
corrected: Crossref records no journal version for arXiv 2105.13402. Mathematically, coarse first step committor equations remain biased under state aggregation, whereas exact coarse committors require the ratio of alpha source sink to equilibrium coarse stationary probabilities Q_m = Pi_m^alpha / (c Pi_m) once finite sliding window weights bar_w_i(S, lambda) relax to stationarity.
math_tex: \bar{w}_i(S,\lambda) = \frac{1}{S - \lambda + 1}\sum_{s=0}^{S-\lambda} w_i(s\Delta t), \qquad Q_m = \frac{\Pi_m^{\alpha}}{c\,\Pi_m} = \frac{\sum_{i \in m}\pi_i q_i}{\sum_{i \in m}\pi_i}

title: Equilibrium Weighted Ensemble spike runs sample 310 opening pathways without converging macroscopic k_open

corrected: Equilibrium Weighted Ensemble over tens of nanoseconds of molecular time stays inside the pre-steady-state transient regime for seconds-timescale spike activation. Estimating steady-state k_open requires terabyte-scale history-augmented Markov postprocessing (Dommer et al. 2022), whereas mean pathway sampling times quantify relative variant readiness rather than rate constants (Kearns et al. 2026).

title: Uniform walker counts per bin fail to guarantee variance reduction below brute force Monte Carlo
paper_label: Aristoff (2022) J. Appl. Probab.
claimed: Conventional Weighted Ensemble simulations assign an equal target count of walkers to every occupied bin along heuristic progress coordinates under the presumption that uniform stratification lowers estimator variance.
corrected: Exact finite population martingale decompositions prove that time average mutation variance scales with squared bin weight divided by bin walker count times intrabin one step Poisson discrepancy variance. Uniform walker counts along poorly aligned bins can exceed brute force Monte Carlo variance, whereas allocating walkers proportional to bin weight times local discrepancy standard deviation approaches the sharp asymptotic lower bound.

title: Steady-state flux permeability P_m = k_DA l_D removes 1D Smoluchowski bias while requiring bulk-water boundaries and dynamic protonation

claimed: Inhomogeneous solubility-diffusion integrals assume memoryless 1D z-diffusion across bilayers, whereas fixed-charge steady-state Weighted Ensemble permeation (P_m = k_DA l_D with acceptor concentration C_A = 0) requires donor and acceptor boundaries outside lipid headgroup wells and freezes ionizable drug charge across the nonpolar membrane core.
corrected: Positioning absorbing acceptor and donor compartments inside flat-potential bulk water ensures k_DA scales inversely with donor slab thickness l_D, and coupling Weighted Ensemble with continuous constant-pH dynamics (Clayton et al. 2026) captures neutral-to-charged protonation shifts absent from fixed-topology tacrine, sotalol, and zacopride runs.

title: Exact Hill relation for equilibrium reaction time requires reactive boundary entry recycling
paper_label: Baudel, Guyader & Lelievre (2023) Stoch. Process. Appl. 155, 393
claimed: Steady state Weighted Ensemble rate derivations invoke 1/MFPT = Flux(A to B | SS) under an unstated assumption of boundary entry independence inside reactant state A, and downstream code cites the 2020 arXiv preprint year rather than the 2023 journal theorem while omitting a primary Hill citation in flux modules.
corrected: For a return process reinjected on boundary A with measure pi, inverse stationary sink flux matches the hitting time initiated from pi. Recovering the equilibrium mean reaction time T_AB requires reinjection from the reactive boundary entry distribution nu_E on boundary A rather than a Boltzmann slice or single basis state, and citations belong to Stoch. title: Weighted Ensemble flux variance bounds require discrepancy variation bins whereas naive coordinates exceed brute force variance
paper_label: Aristoff, Copperman, Simpson, Webber & Zuckerman (2023) J. Chem. Phys. 158, 014108
claimed: Geometric progress coordinates and uniform walker counts per bin are frequently assumed to guarantee lower steady state flux variance and faster transient relaxation than brute force molecular dynamics.
corrected: Asymptotic flux variance reaches the universal lower bound proportional to (int v(x) pi(x) dx)^2 strictly when bins form fine rectangles in flux discrepancy h(x) and local variation v(x) with walker allocation proportional to pi(x)v(x). On the 2D Smoluchowski benchmark, radial bins produce higher variance than brute force dynamics whereas discrepancy bins cut normalized variance by 3 to 5 orders of magnitude.

title: LPATH text string pathway matching remains sensitive to diffusive recrossing loops and shared Weighted Ensemble ancestor branches
paper_label: Bogetti, Leung & Chong (2023) J. Chem. Inf. Model. 63, 7610

corrected: Suarez & Zuckerman 2018 established that diffusive recrossings inflate raw state sequence lengths whereas pure state set distances discard temporal ordering, motivating shortest path fundamental sequences on round trip log transition probabilities. LPATH condenses consecutive state repeats after two stage clustering to separate alanine dipeptide C7eq to C7ax routes (87.5 percent and 12.5 percent), though shared parent segments in Weighted Ensemble trees and non consecutive recrossing loops still perturb route splits.

title: Coarse Markov state models at lag times exceeding the resampling step suffer trajectory merging bias
paper_label: Bose, Kilinc & Dickson (2025) J. Chem. Theory Comput. 21, 1805
claimed: Building discrete time Markov state models from Weighted Ensemble trajectories at lag times longer than the resampling interval presumes standard multi step transition counting monotonically reduces non Markovian error.
corrected: Whenever the Markov lag exceeds the Weighted Ensemble resampling interval, intermediate pruning merges killed walker weights onto non identical surviving conformations inside coarse bins and biases multi step transition counts. Merging bias corrected Markov state models remove pruned weight distortion, shifting the median soluble epoxide hydrolase inhibitor residence time from 0.96 min at single step lag to roughly 50 min against the 27.1 min experimental benchmark.

title: Exact equilibrium coarse Markov transition matrices bias directional steady state fluxes and populations
